project.name: Free Python Center Pivot Survey Mapping Layout Toolkit
project.purpose: Developer-ready handoff for building a local/offline-first Python system that imports survey/imagery/GNSS data, models center pivot irrigation machine geometry, evaluates coverage/conflicts, and exports maps/reports without paid SaaS, paid APIs, or subscription dependencies.
assumptions: The developer will build a local-first application or command-line toolkit; internet access is only used to download free public data, project documentation, package wheels, or GNSS reference data when explicitly requested.
The field technician or user supplies verified machine geometry such as span lengths, overhang length, end-gun throw, tower counts, clearance rules, and machine operating mode.
All acreage, radius, clearance, and machine geometry calculations are performed in a projected coordinate reference system with linear units in meters or feet, not in geographic degrees.
GPS/RTK points may arrive as CSV, GPX, GeoJSON, KML/KMZ, Shapefile, GeoPackage, NMEA logs, RINEX observations, or receiver-specific binary logs.
Free software does not make RTK hardware free. Receivers, antennas, tripods, radios, cellular modems, drones, base stations, and field computers may still cost money.
Real-time RTK corrections are location-specific. Some public/free correction sources exist in some areas, but paid NTRIP/VRS services are excluded as required dependencies.
Imagery-based boundaries are treated as draft or planning-grade unless validated by field survey or RTK ground control.
The output is not a substitute for licensed engineering, hydraulic design, electrical design, utility locating, water-rights/legal review, or manufacturer-specific safety requirements.
non_goals: No paid SaaS, paid cloud processing, paid tile APIs, paid satellite imagery, paid RTK correction services, or trial-only dependencies.
No mandatory Google Maps, Mapbox, Esri/ArcGIS, commercial CAD, or hosted dashboard dependency.
No guarantee of centimeter accuracy without appropriate RTK-capable hardware, base/correction source, antenna setup, field procedure, and quality control.
No automatic machine design approval; technician or engineer review remains required.
No recommendation to scrape OpenStreetMap public tile servers or violate any tile-provider policy.
project.free_cost_policy: Only recommend software, data sources, and workflows that can be run with no purchase, no subscription, no paid API key, and no hidden cloud dependency. Every tool with hardware, correction-service, hosted-service, AGPL/GPL, public-tile, or account/download caveats is flagged. Use permissive open-source packages for the core stack; keep GPL/AGPL tools optional or review-gated. Public datasets are allowed when data access is free, even if a free account, local storage, bandwidth, or processing time is required.
project.confidence_level: High for core package licenses and free-status claims verified from official project pages or package metadata; medium for suitability rankings because field conditions, hardware, local CRS, and manufacturer machine geometry vary. This is not legal advice; commercial distribution should include license review.

core_entities.name: FieldBoundary
core_entities.description: Outer polygon of the farmable or irrigable field, including CRS and survey-quality metadata.

core_entities.name: ObstacleZone
core_entities.description: Polygon/line/point exclusion such as road, ditch, canal, fence, power pole, tree row, building, wetland, no-spray buffer, cemetery, easement, or utility corridor.

core_entities.name: PivotCenter
core_entities.description: Candidate or fixed center point with source type: surveyed, user-entered, optimized, or imported.

core_entities.name: PivotMachine
core_entities.description: Machine geometry: span lengths, tower count, cumulative tower stationing, overhang, end-gun throw, drive direction, min/max angle, allowed speed zones, and clearance buffers.

core_entities.name: SweepMode
core_entities.description: Full-circle, partial-circle, windshield-wiper/reversing arc, sector with shutoff zones, or multiple-sector operation.

core_entities.name: CoverageGeometry
core_entities.description: Polygon representing machine wet area, machine travel/sweep area, end-gun annulus/sector, tower tracks, and clipped irrigated acres.

core_entities.name: SurveyPoint
core_entities.description: Point observation with lat/lon or projected coordinates, timestamp, device/source, fix type, HDOP/PDOP, satellite count, correction age, RMS/accuracy if available, and notes.

core_entities.name: WaterSource
core_entities.description: Well, canal turnout, reservoir, pump station, or hookup point with location and optional elevation/pressure metadata.

core_entities.name: PowerSource
core_entities.description: Electrical service location or generator point used for planning access and utility route.

core_entities.name: PipelineRoute
core_entities.description: Candidate line from water source to pivot, with length, elevation profile, obstacle crossings, and route score.

core_entities.name: LayoutScenario
core_entities.description: One generated or user-specified pivot option containing geometry, metrics, risk flags, inputs, and export layers.

required_inputs: Field boundary in projected CRS or WGS84 coordinates convertible to projected CRS.
Pivot center: fixed surveyed point, user-selected point, or search area for optimization.
Machine geometry: span lengths, overhang, optional end-gun throw, tower count, machine clearance assumptions, and full/partial circle angles.
Obstacles/no-spray/exclusion layers as polygons/lines/points with required buffers.
Target CRS or project location sufficient to choose CRS automatically.
Survey quality requirements: acceptable fix type, HDOP/PDOP, satellite count, correction age, horizontal/vertical accuracy thresholds.
Optional imagery: georeferenced orthomosaic/GeoTIFF, public satellite/aerial imagery, or user-provided raster with ground-control metadata.
Optional terrain/elevation raster for pipeline slope/elevation context.
Optional water source, power source, property line, road access, and preferred pipeline corridor.
computed_outputs: Irrigated acres inside field after clipping to boundary and removing obstacle/no-spray zones.
Coverage percentage by field, parcel, or management zone.
Pivot radius, machine length, overhang radius, end-gun maximum wet radius, and tower cumulative stationing.
Tower locations for selected operating angles and tower-track arcs/circles.
Boundary conflict flags for machine path, overhang, end gun, tower tracks, and clearance buffers.
Obstacle conflict flags and clearance distances.
Partial-circle start/end angles and irrigated sector geometry.
Candidate layout ranking score with acre, conflict, pipe-length, access, and accuracy penalties.
Pipeline route length and optional elevation profile.
Export layers in GeoPackage/GeoJSON/DXF/CSV and static/interactive map artifacts.
layout_calculations: machine_radius = sum(span_lengths) + overhang_length unless manufacturer geometry defines wet radius differently.
end_gun_radius = machine_radius + end_gun_throw; model end-gun as optional annular sector clipped by end-gun shutoff zones.
full_circle_sweep = buffer(pivot_center, machine_radius) in projected CRS.
partial_circle_sweep = sector polygon built from center point and arc points between start_angle and end_angle; handle clockwise/counterclockwise wraparound.
tower_track_i = circle or arc at radius cumulative_span_i around pivot center; buffer track by configured tower/wheel clearance where needed.
clearance conflict = machine_path_or_tower_track_buffer.intersects(obstacle_or_boundary_buffer) when boundary/obstacle is treated as hard clearance.
acres = square_meters / 4046.8564224 or square_feet / 43560 depending project units.
pipeline route score = route_length_cost + obstacle_crossing_penalties + elevation_penalties + constructability flags.
geometry_rules: Never calculate acres, radius, buffer distance, or clearance in EPSG:4326 degrees; reproject to a suitable local projected CRS first.
Validate every polygon before use; repair with shapely.make_valid or controlled buffer(0) fallback, then log the repair.
Close boundary rings, remove duplicate points, reject isolated outliers, and preserve holes for non-irrigable islands.
Represent line obstacles such as roads/fences/ditches as buffered polygons using technician-defined clearances.
Represent point obstacles such as poles/trees/wells as circular buffers using equipment clearance radius.
Use configurable boundary rules: a field edge can be a soft crop boundary for wet-area clipping or a hard fence/property boundary for machine/tower clearance.
Keep wet-area geometry separate from machine-travel geometry because the machine may physically conflict where water coverage would simply be clipped.
Store every layer with CRS metadata and source-quality metadata; reject mixed-CRS layers until transformed.
Use a consistent angular convention: 0 degrees = east or north must be defined explicitly; store clockwise/counterclockwise direction and convert only at rendering boundaries.
When comparing layout scenarios, use the same CRS, same exclusion buffers, same machine geometry, and same scoring weights.
accuracy_considerations: Handheld GPS boundary data is commonly planning-grade, not design-grade; use conservative buffers and field verification.
RTK design-grade points require fixed solution status, adequate satellites, low DOP, low correction age, stable antenna setup, good sky view, repeated observations, and logging of quality metadata.
Base-rover distance, multipath, antenna height entry, datum, epoch, geoid model, and CRS can dominate error even when software is free.
Imagery date and georeferencing error must be recorded; imagery can be stale or offset relative to RTK survey points.
DEM elevation values are usually not accurate enough for final pump/hydraulic design without local survey where grade is critical.
Always store source type: RTK fixed, RTK float, DGPS/SBAS, autonomous GPS, digitized imagery, user-clicked map, imported CAD, or optimized estimate.
When mixing RTK and imagery, use RTK as the higher-trust geometry source for pivot center, boundaries, and hard obstacles.

minimum_viable_stack.purpose: Build a local vector-geometry MVP for GPS boundary import, pivot sweep modeling, acre calculations, obstacle clipping, scenario scoring, static maps, validation, and exports.
Use GeoPackage as the primary project container and GeoJSON/CSV for simple interchange.
For GIS dependencies, conda-forge usually reduces Windows GDAL/GEOS/PROJ installation failures.

advanced_stack.purpose: Add raster/imagery, elevation, CAD/GPX import/export, route planning, and optimization.
Use for validation, local drone photogrammetry, and AI-assisted imagery workflows; review GPL/AGPL obligations before distribution.

rtk_stack.purpose: Support NMEA parsing, live receiver logging, RINEX reading, RTK/PPK processing workflows, NTRIP client software, and receiver QA.
Necessary for centimeter-grade survey, but not guaranteed free. The software handoff must not require paid correction services.
Use archived public GNSS data for PPK/quality workflows where coverage and time windows fit.

imagery_stack.purpose: Use free public imagery/elevation for context, vegetation/terrain screening, and planning layers.
Best free-data path for high-detail field/obstacle analysis when the user already owns imagery/drone data.
Require RTK/GPS validation before using for hard clearance/layout decisions.

visualization_stack.purpose: Static plots, notebook maps, standalone HTML maps/charts, and local dashboards.
Use local/self-hosted basemaps only; do not bulk download or offline-cache public OSM tiles.

testing_stack.purpose: Unit tests, schema validation, style checks, and geometry regression testing.
Prevent hidden geometry and survey-quality failures.

steps: Acquire free/user-owned imagery: NAIP, Sentinel-2, Landsat, drone orthomosaic, or local GeoTIFF. Record source, date, resolution, CRS, and license/terms.
Load raster with rasterio/GDAL; verify geotransform, CRS, bounds, nodata, and resolution.
Reproject imagery to project CRS or reproject vector layers to imagery CRS only for raster operations; keep final layout in local projected CRS.
Clip imagery to field candidate area plus buffer.
For manual or semi-automatic boundary detection, use RGB/NDVI/edge/threshold/contour methods with OpenCV or scikit-image; optionally use Segment Anything for human-in-the-loop masks.
Convert masks/contours to vector polygons with rasterio.features or shapely; simplify and validate geometry.
Digitize or detect obstacle candidates such as roads, ditches, trees, buildings, water, and no-spray zones; buffer according to field rules.
Overlay candidate pivot coverage and machine-travel geometry; compute acres and conflicts.
Mark all imagery-derived boundaries/obstacles as planning-grade until GPS/RTK validation is complete.
Export review map and list of field items needing ground verification.
risks: Imagery may be stale or offset
AI/CV output can misclassify roads, shadows, wet areas, and crop rows
public tile policies may prohibit offline/bulk use
satellite resolution may be too coarse for clearance
validation_checks: Compare imagery boundary against GPS/RTK points
measure known road/building offsets
verify CRS and pixel size
flag imagery older than user threshold
require technician approval before design use

steps: Import boundary points/tracks from CSV, GPX, GeoJSON, KML/KMZ, Shapefile, or GeoPackage.
Parse point attributes: timestamp, fix type, HDOP/PDOP, satellite count, altitude, device, operator notes.
Convert WGS84 coordinates to local projected CRS using pyproj/geopandas.
Remove duplicate points, obvious outliers, and low-quality observations using configurable thresholds.
Build ordered polygon from track or user-provided order; close ring and validate geometry.
Apply boundary cleanup: simplify within survey tolerance, snap near-duplicate vertices, repair invalid topology, preserve holes/exclusions.
Import pivot center, water source, power source, and obstacles as points/lines/polygons; buffer line/point obstacles.
Model full-circle or partial-circle pivot coverage; clip to field and subtract exclusions.
Compute irrigated acres, non-irrigated acres, dry corners, and conflict flags.
Export GeoPackage project, CSV report, DXF plan, and static/interactive map.
risks: KML/GPX altitude datum may be inconsistent
field edge may not equal property/fence boundary
validation_checks: Reject calculations in degrees
confirm polygon area against expected acres
plot point order and boundary path
flag low-quality fixes
require manual review of polygon repairs

steps: Define survey quality threshold: RTK fixed only or accepted fix levels, max HDOP/PDOP, max correction age, min satellites, max horizontal RMS, repeated-shot count, and antenna-height rules.
Collect rover data with RTK-capable hardware; log NMEA/UBX/SBF/RTCM/RINEX where possible with timestamps and quality fields.
If live corrections are used, use free NTRIP client software such as RTKLIB str2str or pygnssutils; do not make a paid correction network a required dependency.
For PPK, collect rover raw observations and base/CORS RINEX data; process with RTKLIB tools and inspect solution status.
Parse NMEA with pynmea2 or GNSS streams with pygnssutils; parse RINEX with georinex for QA; use RTKLIB for actual RTK/PPK solution where needed.
Filter observations by fixed/float/autonomous status and quality metrics; average repeated fixed shots for pivot center and hard obstacles.
Convert final coordinates to project CRS; store datum/epoch/projection metadata.
Use RTK-derived geometry as high-trust source for pivot center, boundary, water source, obstacles, and clearance-critical features.
Generate layout scenarios and export with source-quality metadata visible in the report.
risks: Free NTRIP software does not imply free corrections
wrong antenna height/datum can create large errors
float/autonomous fixes may look precise but fail design threshold
validation_checks: Require fixed solution for design-grade points unless user explicitly downgrades confidence
repeat key points and compare residuals
log correction age and DOP
compare CORS/local base datum
include technician signoff on surveyed pivot center

steps: Create valid field polygon and obstacle/no-spray exclusion polygons in local projected CRS.
Build machine model from validated span lengths, overhang, end-gun throw, and sweep mode.
Generate candidate pivot centers from fixed point, grid search inside field, water-source vicinity, or user-defined allowed area.
For each candidate, generate full-circle or partial-sector sweep, end-gun annulus/sector, tower tracks, and machine-travel clearance geometry.
Clip wet coverage to field and subtract exclusions; evaluate tower/machine conflicts separately.
Score candidate by irrigated acres, dry-corner acres, conflict severity, clearance margin, water/power/pipeline distance, constructability, and survey confidence.
Use coarse grid search first, then refine top candidates with scipy.optimize differential_evolution/minimize or OR-Tools for discrete candidate selection.
Rank scenarios and export maps/tables with explanation of penalties and assumptions.
Require technician review before accepting optimized placement.
risks: Optimizer can find mathematically high coverage but impractical field construction
wrong weights can produce bad recommendations
hard clearance constraints must be separated from wet-area clipping
local optima and geometry repair artifacts
validation_checks: Compare top candidates visually
rerun with different grid/seed
enforce hard constraints before ranking
unit-test known simple fields
report why each rejected scenario failed

field_boundary_processing: Input accepted formats: CSV lat/lon, CSV projected x/y, GPX, GeoJSON, KML/KMZ through GDAL where available, Shapefile, GeoPackage, DXF linework if units/CRS are known.
Normalize to GeoDataFrame with source_crs, target_crs, geometry, point_order, timestamp, quality fields, and source_confidence.
For boundary tracks, preserve recorded order; for unordered points, require user confirmation or compute convex/alpha shape only as draft.
Remove duplicate vertices below tolerance, close ring, detect self-intersections, repair topology, and log all modifications.
Calculate area only after projection. Store acres and square meters/feet plus CRS used.
pivot_center_selection: Modes: fixed_surveyed, user_selected, optimized_grid, optimized_continuous, water_source_constrained.
Reject candidate centers outside allowed center zone unless user explicitly allows off-field center such as corner/wiper designs.
For existing pivots, pivot center should be RTK-surveyed or imported from verified as-built data; imagery-clicked center is planning-grade only.
Candidate center score includes coverage, conflicts, pipeline length, power access, dry corners, and survey confidence.
circle_and_arc_coverage: Use shapely Point(center).buffer(radius, resolution=n) for full-circle approximations; set resolution high enough for acre tolerance.
For sectors, generate arc vertices from start/end angle and construct polygon [center, arc_points..., center].
Use configurable angle convention and store both raw user convention and internal math convention.
Intersections/differences should use prepared/validated geometries where repeated many times.
Store wet coverage and physical machine travel coverage separately.
partial_circle_modeling: Represent windshield-wiper operation as a sector with start_angle, stop_angle, reversal behavior, and optional excluded angle ranges.
Allow separate wet-area sector and physical overhang/tower path sector when end-gun shutoff or span/nozzle package creates different coverage.
Handle 0/360 wraparound and clockwise/counterclockwise input explicitly.
For multiple sectors, union valid sector polygons after building each sector independently.
obstacle_exclusion: Point obstacle -> circular buffer; line obstacle -> width/clearance buffer; polygon obstacle -> original polygon plus safety buffer.
No-spray zone subtraction affects wet coverage; hard obstacle clearance affects machine/tower-travel conflict.
Report nearest clearance distance from tower tracks/overhang path to each obstacle.
Keep source layer, buffer rule, and confidence for every exclusion.
coverage_area_calculation: wet_raw = base_sweep.union(end_gun_sweep if enabled else empty)
dry_acres = field_usable.area - wet_allowed.area converted to acres
coverage_percent = wet_allowed.area / field_usable.area * 100 if field_usable.area > 0 else null
best_fit_optimization: Start with deterministic coarse grid within allowed center zone and radius/angle limits; evaluate all candidates with exact geometry scoring.
Refine top candidates with scipy.optimize.differential_evolution over x, y, radius, start_angle, stop_angle where variables are continuous.
Use penalties for hard conflicts, required clearance failures, radius exceeding machine maximum, unacceptable pipeline crossing, and center outside allowed zone.
Use OR-Tools only for discrete selection problems such as choosing multiple pivots from pre-scored candidates or pipeline network alternatives.
Return not only best score but top N ranked scenarios with score components and rejection reasons.
tower_and_span_modeling: tower_radius_i = cumulative sum of span_lengths through tower i; overhang radius = tower_radius_last + overhang_length.
tower_location(angle, i) = center + tower_radius_i * [cos(angle), sin(angle)] in project CRS units.
tower_track_i = full circle or sector arc at tower_radius_i; buffer by wheel/structure clearance for conflict checking.
Span-to-span clearance can be modeled as swept annular sectors between cumulative radii if needed.
Machine geometry must be based on manufacturer dimensions and field-installed overhang/end-gun package, not guessed.
end_gun_modeling: end_gun_wet = annular sector from machine_radius to end_gun_radius, optionally limited by endgun_on_angles and shutoff zones.
End gun should be separately flaggable as optional, because wind, pressure, nozzle package, and control settings affect real coverage.
Subtract no-spray zones and hard exclusions; show end-gun acres separately from base pivot acres.
Allow end-gun throw and effective wet radius to be scenario inputs, not constants.
multi_pivot_layout: Generate candidate scenarios per pivot; evaluate pairwise overlap and shared obstacles.
Use shapely union of all wet_allowed polygons for total acres; report overlap acres separately.
Use OR-Tools or greedy ranking to choose a set of pivots from precomputed candidates when multiple sites are allowed.
Validate water source capacity and hydraulics outside this geometry MVP.
coordinate_reference_system_handling: Detect input CRS when possible; require user confirmation when missing.
For GPS WGS84, estimate suitable projected CRS from field centroid: UTM zone for broad default; State Plane or local engineering CRS if specified.
Store CRS EPSG/WKT in every layer and in project metadata.
Keep raw coordinates and transformed coordinates for auditability.
Warn when field spans multiple UTM zones or projection distortion exceeds configured tolerance.
accuracy_error_handling: Every geometry should carry source_confidence: rtk_fixed, rtk_float, dgps, autonomous_gps, imagery_digitized, imported_cad, user_estimated, optimized.
Reject or downgrade points with missing quality metadata when design-grade mode is active.
For NMEA GGA, parse GPS quality, number of satellites, HDOP, altitude, geoid separation, and correction age if present.
For u-blox UBX, prefer carrier-solution status and horizontal accuracy estimates where available.
Create QA report that lists all low-confidence inputs and how they affect layout acceptance.

sample_pseudocode.convert_crs:
def convert_crs(gdf, target_crs=None):
    if target_crs is None:
        lon, lat = gdf.to_crs('EPSG:4326').unary_union.centroid.coords[0]
        target_crs = estimate_local_projected_crs(lon, lat)
    projected = gdf.to_crs(target_crs)
    assert projected.crs.is_projected
    return projected
sample_pseudocode.build_field_polygon:
def build_field_polygon(boundary_points, tolerance_m=0.25):
    pts = remove_duplicate_points(boundary_points.geometry, tolerance_m)
    ring = order_points_as_survey_track(pts)
    poly = shapely.geometry.Polygon(ring)
    poly = shapely.make_valid(poly)
    if poly.geom_type == 'MultiPolygon':
        poly = max(poly.geoms, key=lambda g: g.area)
    assert poly.is_valid and poly.area > 0
    return poly

risk_register.mitigation: Reject distance/area calculations unless CRS is projected; auto-select UTM/State Plane only with user confirmation; include CRS in every report.

risk_register.risk: Paid or restricted basemap tile use hidden in UI

risk_register.mitigation: Use local/self-hosted tiles, static user imagery, GeoPackage tiles, or approved free sources; disable bulk tile download; store tile-source terms.

risk_register.mitigation: Mark imagery-derived geometry as planning-grade; require RTK/GPS validation for hard clearance decisions.

risk_register.why_it_matters: GIS stack can fail on Windows or mismatched binary environments, blocking developers.
risk_register.mitigation: Recommend conda-forge environment; pin versions; add smoke tests for geopandas/rasterio/GDAL import and file I/O.

risk_register.risk: GPL/AGPL license obligations in optional tools
risk_register.why_it_matters: QGIS and OpenDroneMap are powerful but GPL/AGPL obligations may affect distribution or networked products.
risk_register.mitigation: Keep permissive core stack separate; use QGIS/ODM as optional validation/local processing tools; legal review before bundling or web deployment.

risk_register.why_it_matters: Mathematical coverage can ignore access, terrain, legal/property lines, hydraulics, utility conflicts, or machine service constraints.
risk_register.mitigation: Separate hard constraints from score weights; show rejection reasons; require technician review and manufacturer/hydraulic validation.

risk_register.why_it_matters: Wrong span lengths, overhang, end-gun throw, or angle limits invalidates all tower and acreage calculations.
risk_register.mitigation: Use Pydantic validation, manufacturer span-chart import, explicit units, checksum of machine config, and technician signoff.

risk_register.risk: RTK quality metadata missing or ignored
risk_register.why_it_matters: Float/autonomous points can pass visually but fail precision requirements.
risk_register.mitigation: Record fix type, DOP, satellites, correction age, RMS/accuracy, antenna height; filter by quality before design-grade use.

risk_register.why_it_matters: Wet-area exclusion and physical machine collision are different rules; mixing them can understate risk.
risk_register.mitigation: Maintain separate wet_exclusion and hard_clearance flags and compute separate conflict reports.

risk_register.risk: Public dataset terms/coverage vary by region
risk_register.why_it_matters: NAIP is U.S.-focused, Sentinel/Landsat resolution may be inadequate, DEM products have regional caveats, and data access may require free accounts.
risk_register.mitigation: Store source/date/license metadata; verify local dataset terms; provide user-supplied imagery/survey fallback.

risk_register.risk: Elevation data used for hydraulic design without survey-grade validation
risk_register.why_it_matters: DEM vertical error, vegetation/buildings, and vertical datum mismatch can mislead pump/pipeline planning.
risk_register.mitigation: Use DEM only for screening; require local survey/engineering for final hydraulic design.

phase_1_minimum_viable_product: Create Python package with data models, CRS module, and vector geometry engine.
Import CSV/GeoJSON/GeoPackage boundary and obstacle layers.
Validate CRS and convert to local projected CRS.
Build full-circle and partial-sector pivot coverage geometry.
Calculate irrigated acres, dry acres, coverage percent, and simple obstacle wet exclusions.
Export GeoPackage, CSV report, and matplotlib plan-view figure.
Implement pytest suite for known acre/geometry scenarios.
phase_2_survey_accuracy: Add GPX/KML/Shapefile imports and robust polygon cleanup.
Add NMEA parser and GPS quality filter with fix type/HDOP/satellites/correction age.
Add repeated-shot averaging and survey QA report.
Add DXF export for pivot center, tower circles, coverage, and obstacles.
Add technician-facing validation checklist and confidence tags.
phase_3_imagery_analysis: Add rasterio/GDAL imagery loading, clipping, and CRS QA.
Add NAIP/Sentinel/Landsat user-download processing notes; no paid APIs.
Add manual/semi-automatic boundary/obstacle vectorization using OpenCV/scikit-image.
Add optional local ODM orthomosaic input path and AGPL warning.
Add imagery source/date/resolution metadata in reports.
phase_4_rtk_integration: Add RTKLIB command wrappers for rnx2rtkp/str2str where installed.
Add georinex RINEX inspection and NetCDF conversion hooks.
Add pygnssutils live stream/NTRIP client integration for free-authorized correction sources.
Add u-blox quality parsing through pyubx2 where applicable.
Add CORS/IGS data workflow documentation and PPK QA report fields.
phase_5_optimization_and_reporting: Add candidate grid search and scipy optimizer refinement.
Add tower-track hard-clearance modeling and separate wet-area/no-spray modeling.
Add pipeline route planning with NetworkX and optional DEM elevation profile.
Add multi-pivot candidate ranking and overlap reporting.
Add local Dash or Jupyter review UI with local/self-hosted basemap safeguards.
Add full scenario report with assumptions, source confidence, conflicts, and acceptance checklist.

acceptance_criteria: The MVP must calculate full-circle coverage acres for a simple square/quarter-section test field within a defined geometric tolerance.
The software must refuse to calculate acres or meter/foot buffers when input geometry is still in EPSG:4326 or another geographic CRS.
The software must preserve and report source confidence for every boundary, obstacle, pivot center, and water-source geometry.
The software must export a valid GeoPackage with layers for field_boundary, obstacles, pivot_center, coverage, dry_corners, tower_tracks, and scenario_metrics.
The software must support at least CSV and GeoPackage input in Phase 1, then GPX/KML/Shapefile/DXF as roadmap items.
The software must include tests for full circle, partial sector, end-gun annulus, obstacle subtraction, no-spray subtraction, and tower-track conflict detection.
The software must include a cost/license report that lists every non-core optional tool and flags GPL/AGPL, tile-policy, hosted-service, and correction-service risks.
The software must not require Google Maps, Mapbox, Esri/ArcGIS, paid RTK corrections, paid satellite imagery, or any hosted cloud service.
The software must allow all calculations to run offline after packages and local data are installed.
The RTK workflow must separate free client/processing software from external hardware/correction-service requirements.
The map UI must not bulk download public OSM tiles and must offer a local/static/self-hosted data path.
The scenario report must show field acres, irrigated acres, dry acres, coverage percent, conflicts, clearances, machine geometry, CRS, source data, and survey-quality flags.

recommended_next_agent_tasks.task: Build a pinned conda-forge environment file
recommended_next_agent_tasks.details: Create environment.yml for Python, numpy, pandas, shapely, geopandas, pyproj, pyogrio, rasterio, matplotlib, pydantic, pytest, ruff; add optional extras for imagery/rtk/ui.
Implement circle/sector/annular-sector generation, coverage clipping, dry-corner calculation, obstacle subtraction, tower tracks, and acres.
Implement CRS detection, local projected CRS selection, EPSG:4326 rejection for distance/area, and unit conversion.
Generate square field, rectangular field, irregular field with holes, partial-sector field, and obstacle collision cases with expected metrics.
Implement CSV and GeoPackage first; then GPX/KML/Shapefile/DXF with clear CRS and quality metadata handling.
Parse NMEA GGA/RMC with pynmea2 and pygnssutils; build filters for fix quality, HDOP, satellites, correction age, and repeated-shot averaging.
Start with grid search and top-N scenario ranking; then add SciPy differential_evolution refinement and hard-constraint penalties.
Generate GeoPackage, CSV metrics, matplotlib PNG, and optional DXF. Include cost/license and source-confidence sections.
Load GeoTIFF with rasterio, clip to field, run simple NDVI/edge/threshold workflows, vectorize candidate masks, and tag results as planning-grade.
Maintain package allowlist with license categories and block paid/API-key dependencies from becoming required.
